title: Tiered liveness contracts and regional dampening for SLO-preserving autoscaler
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: During recent multi-region incidents we observed cascading autoscaler thrashing driven by noisy liveness spikes from short transient failures (disk stalls, transient NVMe GC, brief network blips). Those spikes caused immediate node eviction readyness transitions which in turn triggered aggressive scale-ups in other regions and degraded tail latency — violating the 99th percentile SLO.

Goal: Define and implement a tiered liveness contract + regional dampening layer that: (1) decouples short transient failures from autoscaler decisioning, (2) preserves SLOs for high-priority token classes, and (3) provides predictable multi-region failover behavior with controlled spillover rather than uncontrolled scale thrash.

This ticket covers design, implementation, telemetry, and a staged rollout (canary -> regional -> global) including synthetic load tests against the new behavior. It coordinates with infra, runtime, and SRE teams for safe rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Tiered liveness contract implemented in agent: three levels (soft, firm, critical) with configurable failure windows and hysteresis
Regional dampening controller that applies progressive derating to readiness transitions based on recent eviction rate and cross-region capacity signals
Autoscaler ignores soft-level liveness transitions for up to 30s when token-priority is low; respects firm/critical immediately for high-priority tokens
End-to-end tests demonstrate 40% reduction in autoscaler churn under synthetic transient failure scenarios while keeping P99 latency within SLO for priority traffic
Dashboards show new health envelope metrics (soft-fail % , firm-fail %, dampening factor) and no increase in error rates during canary
Rollout plan documented and rollback knob (force-eval or disable-dampening) validated in canary region
design_notes:
Key ideas and tradeoffs: 
1) Tiered contracts: soft=short transient (e.g. 5s spikes), firm=persistent issues (configurable 30-120s), critical=hard-failure (node OOM/disk offline). Soft events should not trigger autoscaler actions on their own; they should be scored and aggregated by a health window.
2) Regional dampening: when a region observes a sudden rise in soft->firm transitions, apply a progressive dampening multiplier to readiness-to-evict decisions and to autoscaler scale-up weights sent to other regions. This prevents immediate cross-region amplification.
3) Token-priority integration: requests include priority tier; autoscaler logic must favor preserving capacity for high-priority tokens (dedicated weight). Low-priority traffic will be preferred for shedding during dampened windows.
4) Implementation scope: Instrument agent (local health scorer) + central health-aggregator service (lightweight, high-availability) + autoscaler admission changes. Avoid single point of failure by making dampening advisory (agents use local policy if aggregator unavailable).
5) Safety knobs: per-region hard threshold to force node eviction if firm/critical persisted; global kill-switch for dampening disabled via feature flag.

Tradeoffs: Adds complexity to health signal pipeline and requires careful tuning of windows; however benefits in reduced thrash and more predictable SLO outcomes outweigh operational cost for production traffic.
runbook:
Canary plan: 
- Step 0: Deploy agent changes to canary pool (region us-west-2) with dampening disabled but metrics enabled.
- Step 1: Enable soft-tier suppression in canary for low-priority tokens only. Monitor alarms: P99 latency, eviction rate, failure windows.
- Step 2: Enable regional dampening advisory for canary, keep global hard thresholds conservative. Run synthetic transient failure test (disk stall emulator).
- Step 3: If canary stable for 24h with no SLO regressions, expand to 2nd region with traffic shaping.
- Step 4: After 72h without regressions, flip global flag to enable production dampening.
- Rollback: disable dampening flag -> agents revert to previous readiness behavior. If rollback fails, emergency scale policy to cap cross-region scale-ups and divert low-priority tokens to degraded response serving.
- Postmortem triggers: any sustained P99 violation > 30 minutes during rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for health-score computation and tiered windowing (soft/firm/critical)
Integration tests: agent <-> aggregator messaging under network partition (simulate aggregator unavailable)
Chaos test: inject 5-20s disk stalls on subset of nodes while running steady QPS; measure autoscaler events and P99 latency
Synthetic multi-region failover test: cut node bundles in region A to force failover; ensure dampening prevents full cross-region scale thrash
A/B canary with 10% traffic baseline to validate no regression in 24h
metrics: P99 latency for high-priority tokens (goal: no regression)
Autoscaler scale-up/scale-down events per minute (target: -40% churn under transient workload)
Eviction rate and readiness transition histograms by tier (soft/firm/critical)
Dampening factor per-region and cross-region scale weight adjustments
Fraction of requests shed classified by priority
